# pangolin_domain (Resource)

Manages a domain of the provider organization. `wildcard` domains point a wildcard A record at the Pangolin server and are usable at once. `ns` and `cname` domains are delegated to Pangolin and stay unverified until the DNS records listed in `dns_records` exist at your DNS provider; Pangolin then checks them periodically and sets `verified`. `ns` and `cname` require Pangolin Enterprise Edition or Pangolin Cloud: Community Edition only accepts `wildcard`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Wildcard domain: point *.apps.example.com and apps.example.com at the
# Pangolin server. Usable at once; the only type Community Edition
# accepts.
resource "pangolin_domain" "apps" {
  base_domain          = "apps.example.com"
  type                 = "wildcard"
  cert_resolver        = "letsencrypt"
  prefer_wildcard_cert = true
}

# CNAME domain (Enterprise Edition / Pangolin Cloud): create the
# records Pangolin expects at your DNS provider, then wait for
# Pangolin to set `verified`.
resource "pangolin_domain" "portal" {
  base_domain = "portal.example.com"
  type        = "cname"
}

output "portal_dns_records" {
  value = pangolin_domain.portal.dns_records
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `base_domain` (String) The domain name, lowercase (e.g. `example.com` or `apps.example.com`). A `cname` domain cannot be a root domain. Changing it forces a new domain.
- `type` (String) The domain type: `wildcard`, `ns` or `cname`. Changing it forces a new domain.

### Optional

- `cert_resolver` (String) Traefik certificate resolver used for this domain. Only settable for `type = "wildcard"`, where removing it clears the resolver. On `ns` / `cname` domains the server cannot change it after creation, so the provider only reports the server value.
- `prefer_wildcard_cert` (Boolean) Request a wildcard certificate instead of one certificate per subdomain. Only settable for `type = "wildcard"`, where it defaults to `false`. On `ns` / `cname` domains the server cannot change it after creation, so the provider only reports the server value.

### Read-Only

- `config_managed` (Boolean) Whether the domain is declared in the Pangolin config file. Such domains cannot be deleted through the API.
- `dns_records` (Attributes List) DNS records to create at your DNS provider, sorted by record ID. For `wildcard` domains the A records carry the server IP when Pangolin knows it, otherwise a placeholder. Updated on refresh; an in-place update keeps the known records, so `for_each` over them stays plannable. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dns_records))
- `error_message` (String) Last DNS verification error, if any. Updated on refresh.
- `failed` (Boolean) Whether Pangolin stopped retrying the DNS verification. Retry it from the Pangolin UI once the records are fixed. Updated on refresh.
- `id` (String) The domain ID.
- `verified` (Boolean) Whether Pangolin has verified the domain's DNS records. Always `true` for `wildcard` domains. Updated on refresh.

<a id="nestedatt--dns_records"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dns_records`

Read-Only:

- `base_domain` (String) Record name.
- `record_type` (String) Record type: `NS`, `CNAME`, `A` or `TXT`.
- `value` (String) Record value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Domains import by domain ID. Look it up with the pangolin_domains
# data source or in the Pangolin web UI.
#
# Note: a domain declared in the Pangolin config file (config_managed
# = true) cannot be deleted through the API; `terraform destroy` then
# fails until it is removed from the config file or from the state.
terraform import pangolin_domain.example <domain_id>
```
